x: WTO stands for World Trade Organization, set up in 1995 with its head office in Geneva.
t: Expand the short name.

x: Option C is incorrect: the WTO began on 1 January 1995, under the Marrakesh Agreement signed in 1994. Its head office is in Geneva.
t: Discriminate the year signed from the year it began.

x: Both are true: the WTO is wider than GATT because it covers goods, services, intellectual property and investment, while GATT dealt mainly with goods. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the coverage explains the breadth.

x: GATT was signed on 30 October 1947 in Geneva by 23 founding parties and came into force in 1948. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Match each GATT fact to its value.

x: I and II are correct: the WTO grew out of GATT's Uruguay Round, and GATT focused on cutting tariffs and quotas. III and IV are false because they swap the dates: GATT dates from 1948 and the WTO from 1995.
t: Watch for swapped dates.

x: GATT stands for General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade. The traps swap in 'Arrangement', 'Global' or 'Association'.
t: Expand the short name.

x: Both are true: the WTO replaced GATT, and it is an international trade organisation. Being an organisation does not explain why it replaced GATT, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a nature explains a replacement.

x: Both are true: GATT was an agreement among countries, while the WTO is a permanent international organisation.
t: Discriminate an agreement from an organisation.

x: The Uruguay Round of GATT ran from 1986 to 1993 and led to the WTO's creation in 1995.
t: Recall the Uruguay Round years.

x: Option C is incorrect: TRIPS is Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights. Trade-Related Investment Measures is TRIMS, and services is GATS.
t: Discriminate TRIPS from TRIMS.

x: Both are true: Green Box support is allowed because it causes little or no trade distortion. R explains A.
t: Ask whether low distortion explains permission.

x: The Green Box causes little or no distortion, the Amber Box is distorting support subject to limits, and the Blue Box is Amber-type support with production limits. The answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i.
t: Remember the traffic-light boxes.

x: Three are Green Box: decoupled income support, environmental programmes and farmer training. Price support is Amber Box.
t: Find the trade-distorting item.

x: The Uruguay Round extended trade rules beyond goods, through GATS (services), TRIPS (intellectual property) and TRIMS (investment measures). The answer is a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.
t: Expand each agreement's name.

x: All three are correct: regional development, farm research, and pest and disease control are all Green Box support.
t: Recall the Green Box examples.

x: Both are true: production-linked subsidies are Amber Box because the Amber Box covers support that distorts trade or production and is subject to limits. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the definition explains the example.

x: The IMF and the World Bank are both headquartered in Washington, D.C. The WTO is in Geneva.
t: Match each institution to its city.

x: Option C is incorrect: the IMF was formally set up on 27 December 1945, after being planned at Bretton Woods in 1944. India was a founding member.
t: Discriminate the year planned from the year set up.

x: Both are true: the IMF helps members with balance-of-payments problems because such problems are the main focus of its lending. R explains A.
t: Ask whether the focus explains the function.

x: The reserve tranche is an unconditional drawing right, the RFI gives fast help for urgent BoP needs, the RCF gives soft help to low-income countries, and the IMF's core task is surveillance. The answer is a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii.
t: Match each IMF tool to its purpose.

x: I, II and IV are correct: the IMF promotes monetary stability, gives technical help, and lends for BoP problems. III is false because project finance is the World Bank's job.
t: Discriminate the IMF from the World Bank.

x: The IMF is an international monetary institution, India a founding member, the RFI is open to IMF members, and the World Bank is a Bretton Woods institution. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Match each item to its description.

x: Option C is incorrect: lending for balance-of-payments problems is the IMF's role. The World Bank funds development projects.
t: Discriminate the IMF from the World Bank.
